| # Decisions log. 2026-10-28: written up as ADR 0111 (proposed) with a reference service (`src/sample-service/`), a service kit and a CI check that builds each service image and checks health, JSON logs, clean shutdown and config errors |

Status key: Decided (Didi confirmed), Proposed (written down, needs Didi's confirmation), Open (needs a decision, with who decides).

Dates are the day Didi decided. "By Oct 27" means decided in the planning sessions before Oct 28.

## 1. Decided

### Decided by Oct 27, 2026

| ID    | Decision                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| D-001 | Windmill is the runner. Linear is a mirror, and our own state store is the source of truth                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| D-002 | Two machines: Machine 1 (idea) and Machine 2 (work item). Machine 3 (daily scan) comes later and feeds Machine 1                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| D-003 | A deterministic runner owns every transition. Agents never move themselves. Every state has one owner role                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| D-004 | Bots are shared across all projects. Agents a bot dispatches are scoped to one project. The Council is shared. Expect 6 to 10 projects                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| D-005 | Escalation goes to the Council first, then to Didi only if the Council cannot resolve it                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| D-006 | Gates: approve-once (new secrets or permissions, dropping data, DNS changes each approved separately, PII access), only-Didi (spending money, personal messages and emails, production deploys, playbook rule changes), and visual approval for design. Free to run: job applications and forms, code, docs, staging deploys, internal tickets |
| D-007 | Production deploys in v1: Didi reviews staging each morning and approves the deploy on GitHub from his phone                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| D-008 | Scope: any new feature, new or changed user flow, or changed product direction goes to Didi. The Council decides priority, tech and architecture, naming and branding, and user-facing copy unless it changes approved direction                                                                                                               |
| D-009 | Done means: tests pass and CI green, matches the approved design (UI), docs updated or no docs impact stated, works on staging checked by a bot. Playbook proposals never block Done                                                                                                                                                           |
| D-010 | Nothing sits idle. If nothing blocks an item, the runner dispatches it immediately. Continue by default                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| D-011 | Spend alerts at a threshold and work keeps going. A looping item stops and goes to the Council. No daily cap                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| D-012 | The attention list is a table in the state store in v1. Channels only render it. A frontend comes later and the system builds it                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| D-013 | The state store is a relational database with node and edge tables. A graph database is not required                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| D-014 | Every new idea starts with an Interview of Didi (one question at a time, answers verbatim with the time) before any planning or building                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| D-015 | Build order: dogfood. The first project through the system is the system itself                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

| O-61 | How the OpenCode image's wrapper opens the run's PR and posts its docs note (D-235, N-44) **Decided 2026-11-02 by the implementing agent (PR and docs note slice).**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | The model's final message must end with exactly one fenced block with the info string `foreman-report`, holding one JSON object with exactly `pullRequestTitle` (one line, 1 to 200 characters) and `docsNote` (`{"impact": "none"}`, optionally with a `note`, or `{"impact": "updated", "note": "..."}`, the `docs_note` payload of docs/guards.md). The check is strict: no block, two blocks, an unclosed block, text that is not that object, an unknown field, or `updated` with no note fails the run, and nothing is guessed. The rest of the message, with every credential value removed, is the PR's description; the title comes from the block, since the task has no title for a PR. The instructions in `contracts/bots/developer.yaml` and `designer.yaml` show the block, and a test parses their example. After a successful run the wrapper, in this order: reads the block; reads the run's branch on GitHub (the model clones and pushes with git, so the wrapper never pushes and never reads the checkout), which fails the run as "nothing was pushed" when it is missing and gives the head commit; lists the open PRs whose head is that branch in the same repository and reuses the one it finds; otherwise reads the default branch and opens a PR into it. A closed or merged PR is never reused (after a merge, the next round needs a new PR from the same branch). A 422 on opening lists once more and reuses a PR opened in between; more than one open PR for the branch fails the run. Then it posts `docs_note` to `POST /reports` with the run's state API token, `ref` set to the PR link built from the repository and number. Any failed step makes the result `error` with a fixed start naming the step (`FINISH_FAILURES`), which the runtime maps to `fail`; texts name the step and GitHub's status only, never a body, the branch or a token. A success result carries `structured.pullRequest` (number, link, head commit, reused) and `structured.docsNote.impact`: the done report naming the PR. No evidence id is passed on (a database id). The runner still links the PR from GitHub's events by branch and App author and reads the note from the state store, never from this result. The task file now carries `nodeId` and `branch` (`runBranch`) for the Developer and Designer, and the task check requires both; the image requires `FOREMAN_REPOSITORY`, `HTTPS_PROXY` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` before OpenCode starts. GitHub is reached by a CONNECT tunnel to `api.github.com:443` through the run's egress proxy, in plain Node code (no new package and not Node's experimental proxy switch), with TLS to GitHub inside the tunnel. No egress change: `api.github.com` is already in both bot files' `allowed_hosts` and the state API is the proxy's `/state-api` route (D-195). A run that stops for a product decision without pushing now fails as "nothing was pushed".
